editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 12 keeps the "modest deviation → calibration" and "severe TLS → strategy change, possibly pausing" conditions, and entry 16 keeps the "only affected qubits/gates plus batching-rule qubits" scope and the "under two hours per day" figure. Two small issues remain. In entry 44, "100큐비트" uses the Hangul form while the rest of the page writes qubit in Latin letters, and the "사슬(체인)" gloss reads clunky. In entry 12, the trailing "…감소할 때까지 유지됩니다" has no clear subject, so it is unclear what is kept in place.

examples.source: for the best 100-qubit length string
examples.translation: 최적의 100큐비트 길이 사슬(체인) 기준
examples.suggested: 최적의 100-qubit 길이 체인 기준
examples.why: '큐비트' is the only Hangul rendering of qubit in a file that uses qubit/Qubit everywhere else. The doubled gloss '사슬(체인)' is also stiffer than a single term.

examples.source: might be automatically modified (and could include pausing calibrations) until such TLS activity decreases back to acceptable levels
examples.translation: …자동으로 수정될 수 있으며(캘리브레이션 일시 중지가 포함될 수도 있습니다), TLS 활동이 허용 수준으로 감소할 때까지 유지됩니다.
examples.suggested: …TLS 활동이 허용 수준으로 다시 감소할 때까지 자동으로 수정될 수 있습니다(캘리브레이션 일시 중지가 포함될 수도 있습니다).
examples.why: Splitting 'until' into a separate clause ending in '유지됩니다' leaves it unclear what is kept in place. Attaching '까지' directly to the modification reads more naturally and matches the English structure.

editor_note: The translation is accurate and reads naturally. 'changelog' is rendered as '변경 로그' and 'skill' as '스킬' throughout, and entry [5] keeps the meaning that the skill was released for migrating `qiskit-ibm-runtime` code ('...코드 마이그레이션을 위해 릴리스되었습니다').

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still fix two small things. Entry 3 renders the product name as "Qiskit Transpiler Service 클라이언트", while entries 0, 1, 6 and 8 on the same page keep "Qiskit Transpiler Service client" in English, so the file is inconsistent. Entry 9 turns "Perhaps most importantly" into "무엇보다도" and drops the hedge "perhaps", which makes the claim slightly stronger. The rest of entry 9 is faithful: "might be faster" is correctly hedged as "더 빠르고 더 나은 결과를 낼 수 있는", and the 트랜스파일러 패스 terminology is correct. Entry 4 ("2026년 1월") is correct.

examples.source: Qiskit Transpiler Service client v0.15.2
examples.translation: Qiskit Transpiler Service 클라이언트 v0.15.2
examples.suggested: Qiskit Transpiler Service client v0.15.2
examples.why: Entries 0, 1, 6 and 8 keep 'client' in English as part of the product name. Rendering it as 클라이언트 only in this heading makes the page inconsistent.

examples.source: Perhaps most importantly, the service invites users to experiment with...
examples.translation: 무엇보다도 이 서비스를 통해 새롭고 개선된 AI 기반 트랜스파일러 패스를 직접 실험해 볼 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 아마도 가장 중요한 점은, 이 서비스를 통해 새롭고 개선된 AI 기반 트랜스파일러 패스를 직접 실험해 볼 수 있다는 것입니다.
examples.why: The hedge 'perhaps' is dropped, so the claim becomes slightly stronger. The meaning otherwise holds.

editor_note: Entry 10 is faithful and natural: "joint projective measurement" is rendered as "결합 사영 측정", "unlocking compilation to Pauli-based computation" as "Pauli 기반 계산으로 컴파일할 수 있습니다", and "a common representation in fault-tolerant quantum computing" keeps its apposition as "결함 허용 양자 컴퓨팅에서 흔히 쓰이는 표현 방식". The ending uses 합니다체, the same as the rest of the page, including entries 8 and 11.

All three rewritten entries are accurate and natural 해요체. In [17] and [18], "Account notice를 확인하고 **Continue**를 클릭하세요" is a reasonable Korean UI rendering of "Complete the ... notice", and [32] renders "three-dot menu" as "점 3개(⋮) 메뉴", which is a clear and faithful choice.

The Korean prose in rewritten entry 21 is faithful and natural. "반환된 bearer 토큰을 복사하여 저장하세요" and "요청 헤더에 CRN과 bearer 토큰을 포함하여 … 요청을 인증하세요" keep every element of the English, and bearer 토큰 matches entry 20. The problem is that the rewrite dropped the leading whitespace. The "Copy and save" line moved from 4 spaces of indent to 2, and the "1. Authenticate" list item moved from 2 spaces to column 0. After a fenced code block these lines can no longer continue the nested list item, so the step list will probably render broken or renumbered. The meaning is intact, but the source indentation should be restored.

editor_note: Both rewritten link labels are faithful and conventional: dynamical decoupling became '동적 디커플링', and Pauli twirling became 'Pauli 트월링', which matches '측정 트월링' and '게이트 트월링' elsewhere on the page.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: entry 5 keeps "any paid plan" as "모든 유료 플랜에서" and renders SLO/SLA as "서비스 수준 목표/계약", and entry 9 uses "영역 장애" and "남아 있는 HA 인스턴스 노드", matching "영역" for zone in entry 8.
Both rewritten entries are faithful 해요체 with nothing lost: entry 5 is "설치하기 전에 다음 가이드의 지침을 따르세요", and entry 9 keeps "주기적으로 확인하세요" and the recommendation to "자주 업데이트할 것을 권장합니다".

The meaning is accurate throughout. I found no drift in the conditions, caveats, precedence rules (num_randomizations * shots_per_randomization over shots), the PUB-grouping example or the TREX exception, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The page is written entirely in formal 합니다체 (설명합니다, 제공합니다) instead of the project's 해요체 convention. Three terms are rendered inconsistently: 'primitive' is 'Primitive' in [0]/[5]-[8] but '프리미티브' in the tables [20]/[22]; 'precision' is 'precision 값' in [22] but '정밀도' in [37]; 'dictionary' is '딕셔너리' in [20]/[22] but 'dictionary' in [43]. There are also small calques: 'consequences' is rendered as the ambiguous '결과' in [54], and the bold heading in [38] is awkwardly split.

examples.source: This guide describes how to migrate ...
examples.translation: ...마이그레이션하는 방법을 설명합니다.
examples.suggested: ...마이그레이션하는 방법을 설명해요.
examples.why: The whole page uses formal 합니다체, but the project convention is 해요체.

examples.source: Mixed precision values in a single job are no longer supported.

examples.source: You must account for the following consequences when constructing the local PUB
examples.translation: 로컬 PUB를 구성할 때 다음과 같은 결과를 고려해야 합니다.

examples.translation: PUB당 하나의 작업이 아니라 대상 값별로 PUB를 그룹화하세요. 서로 다른 값마다 하나의 작업입니다.

examples.why: The trailing '서로 다른 값마다 하나의 작업입니다.' is a stiff fragment that reads like a calque of the em-dash.

editor_note: All 8 rewritten entries match their English and read naturally in 해요체. Terms are consistent: the verb uses 트랜스파일, the noun uses 트랜스파일레이션, and entry 23 keeps the 인증 없이도 caveat.

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning and nothing in them would mislead a learner. "The first IBM Quantum primitives", the error-mitigation example and the hardware-access claim in entry 3 are all accurate, and each item in the entry 9 list is carried over. One term is inconsistent: the same linked concept (/guides/primitives) is "Primitives 기본 클래스" in entry 3 but "프리미티브 기본 클래스" in entry 9, and entry 9 also writes "IBM Quantum primitives" and "Primitives" in the same list. Entry 3 also uses the formal -습니다 endings (만들어졌습니다, 구현체입니다, 사용됩니다) rather than the 해요체 used in entry 9's imperatives, which is a small register slip.

examples.source: Learn about the [primitive base classes](/guides/primitives) that the IBM Quantum primitives are based on.
examples.translation: IBM Quantum primitives의 기반이 되는 [프리미티브 기본 클래스](/guides/primitives)에 대해 알아보세요.
examples.suggested: IBM Quantum Primitives의 기반이 되는 [Primitives 기본 클래스](/guides/primitives)에 대해 알아보세요.
examples.why: Entry 3 renders the same linked term as 'Primitives 기본 클래스'. Here it becomes '프리미티브', and the same list switches between 'primitives' and 'Primitives'. It should be spelled one way throughout the file.

examples.source: Primitives were created to simplify the most common tasks ... and are used to access IBM Quantum® hardware.
examples.translation: ...단순화하기 위해 만들어졌습니다. ... 구현체입니다. ... 하드웨어에 접근하는 데 사용됩니다.
examples.suggested: ...단순화하기 위해 만들어졌어요. ... 구현체예요. ... 하드웨어에 접근하는 데 사용돼요.
examples.why: The project uses 해요체, but this rewrite uses formal -습니다 endings. It is a minor register slip.

editor_note: All five rewritten entries are faithful and natural, e.g. "stochastic" rendered as 확률론적 with the no-guarantee caveat intact (11), and the calibrated-default-basis-gate logic plus the cx/ecr example preserved in 40 ("캘리브레이션이 완료된 Gate이므로 추가 명령어/펄스 Gate를 제공할 필요가 없습니다").
Rewritten entry 6 is faithful and natural in 해요체 ("생성 중인 Circuit을 확인하는 것이 종종 유용합니다… 다음 옵션을 사용하세요"), and it uses Circuit the same way as the rest of the page.

Entry 12 (the Credly privacy notice) is accurate and would not mislead anyone. It keeps the data shared (name, email address, badge earned), Credly's US location, and the hedge in "may share … globally" (전 세계의 … 공유할 수 있습니다). A native editor would still change two things. "IBM 디지털 배지를 발급하려면 … 공유됩니다" uses the conditional -려면 with no matching subject, so it reads like "if you want to issue a badge"; 발급하기 위해 expresses the English purpose clause. The notice is also written in the formal 귀하/합니다 style instead of the site's 해요체. That choice is defensible for legal text, and nearby entries 7–9 use 합니다 too.

examples.source: In order to issue you an IBM Digital Badge, your personal information (name, email address, and badge earned) will be shared with Credly.
examples.translation: IBM 디지털 배지를 발급하려면 귀하의 개인 정보(이름, 이메일 주소, 획득한 배지)가 Credly에 공유됩니다.
examples.suggested: IBM 디지털 배지를 발급하기 위해 귀하의 개인 정보(이름, 이메일 주소, 획득한 배지)가 Credly와 공유됩니다.
examples.why: -려면 is a conditional ('if you want to issue') and has no matching subject in a passive sentence. -기 위해 expresses the purpose in the English and reads naturally.

examples.source: NOTICE: IBM leverages the services of Credly...
examples.translation: 공지: IBM은 ... 지원합니다. ... 확인할 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: Optionally align to 해요체 (e.g. 확인할 수 있어요) or keep formal consistently as a legal notice
examples.why: The page convention is 해요체. The formal 귀하/합니다 style is defensible for a legal privacy notice, so this is a minor note only.

editor_note: Entry 11 is faithful: the modal "may share" survives as "공유할 수 있습니다", the personal-data list (이름, 이메일 주소, 획득한 배지) is complete, and "제3자 데이터 처리업체" is correct; the formal 합니다체 with 귀하 suits a legal notice and matches the rest of the page.

The rewritten heading in entry 20, "유일 해 검색", has the right meaning (a search with a single solution) and would not mislead a learner. The problem is the word for "search": it uses 검색, but the same page says 탐색 in entry 32 ("탐색하는 항목"). Korean CS and quantum-algorithm writing normally uses 탐색 for search problems, while 검색 suggests retrieval or web search. The heading also doesn't clearly point to the problem that entry 21 names as *Unique search*, so "유일 해 탐색" would fit the page better.

examples.source: Unique search {#unique-search}
examples.translation: 유일 해 검색 {#unique-search}
examples.suggested: 유일 해 탐색 {#unique-search}
examples.why: The word for 'search' doesn't match the rest of the page: entry 32 uses 탐색 for searching over items, and 탐색 is the standard Korean CS word for a search problem. 검색 reads as information retrieval. The meaning is still correct.

editor_note: All 8 rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 135 renders "its inverse (or, equivalently, conjugate transpose)" correctly as 역연산(즉, 켤레 전치), and entry 179 keeps the emphasis on doubling (*두 배*). The one problem is register: entries 211 and 221 end in the plain declarative "~한다고 하자", while the rest of the page uses polite -습니다/-요 endings. They should be changed to "~한다고 합시다" or "~한다고 가정해 보겠습니다".

examples.source: Suppose that $\theta$ is a real number and $y\in \{0,\ldots,2^m-1\}$ satisfies

examples.suggested: $\theta$가 실수이고 $y\in \{0,\ldots,2^m-1\}$가 다음을 만족한다고 가정해 보겠습니다.
examples.why: This uses the plain '하자' ending on a page that otherwise uses polite -습니다/-요 endings, so it breaks the page's register.

examples.translation: 이제 $y\in \{0,\ldots,2^m-1\}$가 다음을 만족한다고 하자.
examples.suggested: 이제 $y\in \{0,\ldots,2^m-1\}$가 다음을 만족한다고 가정해 보겠습니다.
examples.why: Same register slip as entry 211: the plain '하자' ending doesn't match the polite register used across the rest of the page.

editor_note: None of the 12 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Conditions, quantities and caveats all match the English, including "unitary only if f invertible", "k = max of workspace counts" and "at the cost of larger circuits". Entry 24 uses "상위 n개 Qubit" for the physically top qubits. Right after entry 9 explains that the top qubits are the least significant, "상위" (which usually means high-order) can make this unclear, so "위쪽 n개" is safer. Entry 51 has the awkward "우리가 이미 방법을 모르는 함수" and the stiff "답은 그렇다입니다". In entry 29, "*garbage(쓰레기)*의" puts the closing asterisk between ")" and a Hangul letter, so the emphasis may not render. Entry 9 also glosses the same idea twice with "자릿값(유효 자릿수)".

examples.source: the n input bits of C correspond to the top n qubits of R
examples.translation: $C$의 $n$개 입력 비트가 $R$의 상위 $n$개 Qubit에 대응하고
examples.suggested: $C$의 $n$개 입력 비트가 $R$의 위쪽 $n$개 Qubit에 대응하고
examples.why: This means position in the diagram. In Korean, '상위' usually means high-order or significance, which here is the opposite of Qiskit's convention (top = least significant) that the page explained just before.

examples.source: So, this isn't a shortcut for computationally inverting functions when we don't already know how to do that!
examples.translation: 따라서 이것은 우리가 이미 방법을 모르는 함수를 계산적으로 역산하는 지름길은 아닙니다!
examples.suggested: 따라서 이것은 역함수를 계산하는 방법을 아직 모르는 함수를 역산하게 해 주는 지름길이 아닙니다!
examples.why: '이미 방법을 모르는' is a calque of 'don't already know' and reads awkwardly. Also, '답은 그렇다입니다' is stiff; '답은 "그렇다"입니다' reads better.

examples.source: it's short for *garbage.*
examples.translation: 그것은 *garbage(쓰레기)*의 약자이기 때문입니다.
examples.suggested: 그것은 *garbage*(쓰레기)의 약자이기 때문입니다.
examples.why: A closing '*' between ')' and a Hangul letter is not right-flanking in CommonMark, so the emphasis may render as literal asterisks.

examples.source: the qubits are ordered in increasing significance from top to bottom
examples.translation: Qubit이 위에서 아래로 자릿값(유효 자릿수)이 커지는 순서로 정렬됨
examples.suggested: Qubit이 위에서 아래로 갈수록 자릿값이 커지는 순서로 정렬됨
examples.why: The parenthetical repeats the same idea, which adds clutter inside a sentence that is already in parentheses.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. [47] and [49] render "if and only if" as "필요충분조건은 … 양의 반정부호인 것입니다", which keeps both directions of the condition, and "for every a" stays "모든 a에 대해". The term 양의 반정부호 matches its other uses in the file, including [76] and [96].

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning. Entry 9 renders density matrices as 밀도 행렬, channels as 채널 and measurements as 측정, which are correct. Its only flaw is the hedge "조작적인(실질적인) 의미에서": 조작적 is the standard rendering of "operational", and the gloss 실질적인 ("practical/substantive") is a looser, slightly different sense that a native editor would drop. Entry 12 adds 모두 ("all the lessons"), a small strengthening that is not in the English; it is harmless but not faithful.

examples.source: how they relate to channels and measurements in operational ways
examples.translation: 이것이 채널 및 측정과 조작적인(실질적인) 의미에서 어떻게 관련되는지도 논의합니다
examples.suggested: 이것이 조작적(operational) 관점에서 채널 및 측정과 어떻게 관련되는지도 논의합니다
examples.why: 조작적 is the conventional term for 'operational'. The parenthetical 실질적인 is a hedge gloss with a different nuance ('practical/substantive'), and it reads like translator uncertainty.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: 이 시험은 본 과정의 레슨을 모두 읽은 뒤에 응시하는 것을 전제로 합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 시험은 본 과정의 레슨을 읽은 뒤에 응시하도록 구성되어 있습니다.
examples.why: 모두 ('all') is not in the source and slightly strengthens the recommendation. 전제로 합니다 is also a bit stiff.

editor_note: Entry 8 is faithful and reads naturally. It renders 'fidelity' as 충실도 and 'trace (Tr)' as 대각합(Tr), both consistent with the rest of the page, and keeps the conventional math phrasing '밀도 행렬이라고 합시다'.

Entry 36 keeps the English meaning. It correctly says the Estimator setting is limited to 0/1 with 1 as the default, that other contexts allow 0-3, and that optimization is set to 0 with skip_transpilation because the circuit was already transpiled with the pass manager. The last sentence copies English word order, though: "여기서, 우리는 실제로 … 사용할 것입니다. 왜냐하면 우리는 … Transpile했기 때문입니다." splits a "because" clause into a separate 왜냐하면 sentence and repeats 우리는, which reads like machine translation. "많은 맥락에서 (Estimator 포함)" is also a stiff literal rendering of "In many contexts (Estimator included)".

examples.source: Here, we will actually set optimization to 0, and use 'skip\_transpilation = true', because we have already transpiled our circuit using the pass manager above, in the optimization section.
examples.translation: 여기서, 우리는 실제로 최적화를 0으로 설정하고 'skip\_transpilation = true'를 사용할 것입니다. 왜냐하면 우리는 위의 최적화 섹션에서 Pass Manager를 사용하여 이미 우리의 회로를 Transpile했기 때문입니다.
examples.suggested: 위의 최적화 섹션에서 Pass Manager로 회로를 이미 트랜스파일했으므로, 여기서는 최적화를 0으로 설정하고 'skip\_transpilation = true'를 사용합니다.
examples.why: Splitting off a 왜냐하면 sentence and repeating 우리는/우리의 is a calque of English syntax. A Korean technical writer would put the reason first as a -(으)므로 clause.

examples.source: In many contexts (Estimator included), settings are limited to 0 and 1
examples.translation: 많은 맥락에서 (Estimator 포함), 설정은 0과 1로 제한되며
examples.suggested: Estimator를 비롯한 많은 경우에 설정값은 0과 1만 가능하며
examples.why: '많은 맥락에서 (… 포함)' copies the English parenthetical word for word and reads stiffly.

editor_note: None of the 14 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. The math, conditions and claims match the English, including the Estimator paragraph (67), the geometry answer (111), the ADAPT-VQE caveats (133) and the QSCI workflow (147). There are still a few things a native editor would fix. In entry 74, "algorithms we will discuss in this course" became "이 과정에서 나중에 다룰", but 과정 already means "process" earlier in the same paragraph, so the sentence is ambiguous. Entry 74 also drops "for example", so spin systems read as the only case. In entry 128, "lesson" is rendered as 강의, while the file uses 단원 for lesson and 강의 for the course (137). Entry 133 mixes 매개변수화 and 파라미터 in one sentence and uses 지역 최솟값 where entry 68 has 국소 최솟값. Entry 40 uses 노이즈 while entry 132 uses 잡음 for the same concept.

examples.source: But chemical systems may be better suited to some of the other algorithms we will discuss in this course.
examples.translation: 하지만 화학 시스템은 이 과정에서 나중에 다룰 다른 알고리즘들에 더 적합할 수도 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 하지만 화학 시스템에는 이 강좌에서 나중에 다룰 다른 알고리즘들이 더 적합할 수도 있습니다.
examples.why: 과정 already means 'process' earlier in this paragraph (이 과정이 유용할 수 있습니다), so '이 과정에서' is ambiguous. 강좌 matches the rest of the file. The dropped 'for example' in the spin-systems sentence (e.g. 상호작용하는 스핀 시스템이 그 예입니다) should also be restored.

examples.source: The original VQE algorithm described throughout this lesson uses a predefined, fixed ansatz
examples.translation: 이 강의 전반에 걸쳐 설명한 원래의 VQE 알고리즘은
examples.suggested: 이 단원 전반에 걸쳐 설명한 원래의 VQE 알고리즘은
examples.why: The file uses 단원 for 'lesson' (entries 5, 22, 38) and 강의 for 'course' (137). Using 강의 here blurs lesson and course.

examples.source: it may suffer from over-parameterization ... parameter optimization with many gate structures.
examples.translation: 과잉 매개변수화 문제가 발생할 수도 있습니다. 또한 기울기 계산과 다양한 Gate 구조에 대한 파라미터 최적화가 필요하기 때문에
examples.suggested: 과잉 매개변수화 문제가 발생할 수도 있습니다. 또한 기울기 계산과 다양한 Gate 구조에 대한 매개변수 최적화가 필요하기 때문에
examples.why: Within one sentence it switches between 매개변수 and 파라미터. It also says 지역 최솟값 where entry 68 has 국소 최솟값.

examples.source: **Scalability and Noise Robustness**
examples.translation: **확장성 및 잡음 견고성**
examples.suggested: **확장성 및 노이즈 견고성**
examples.why: Rewritten entry 40 uses 노이즈 for 'noise' and this entry uses 잡음. The concept is still clear, but one term should be chosen.

editor_note: Every entry keeps the English meaning. Suppression, mitigation, detection and correction are rendered as 억제/완화/감지/정정, quantum advantage as 양자 우위, and "time-released" correctly as 순차적으로 공개. The file breaks the 해요체 convention, though. [4] and [6] are written in formal 합니다체 (살펴봅니다, 논의합니다, 주목합니다, 개발 중입니다, 준비될 예정입니다) where the convention calls for 살펴봐요/논의해요/개발 중이에요. The description [0] also stacks "위한" twice ("활용하기 위한 … 처리를 위한"), which reads as a stiff calque.

examples.source: Explore modern tools for handling noise and errors to get the most out of quantum computers.
examples.translation: 양자 컴퓨터를 최대한 활용하기 위한 노이즈 및 오류 처리를 위한 최신 도구를 살펴보세요.
examples.suggested: 양자 컴퓨터를 최대한 활용할 수 있도록 노이즈와 오류를 다루는 최신 도구를 살펴보세요.
examples.why: Two stacked '위한' clauses read as a calque of the English structure.

examples.source: This course explores the tools being used in the pursuit of quantum advantage...
examples.translation: 이 코스에서는 ... 도구들을 살펴봅니다. ... 논의합니다. ... 특히 주목합니다.
examples.suggested: 이 코스에서는 ... 도구들을 살펴봐요. ... 논의해요. ... 특히 주목해요.
examples.why: The project convention is 해요체, but this paragraph is written in formal 합니다체.

examples.source: The exam and badge for this course are still under development.
examples.translation: 이 코스의 시험과 배지는 아직 개발 중입니다. ... 준비될 예정입니다.
examples.suggested: 이 코스의 시험과 배지는 아직 개발 중이에요. ... 준비될 예정이에요.
examples.why: This entry is also in formal 합니다체 instead of the 해요체 convention.

editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout, and the core terms are correct and used consistently: 오류 억제/완화/감지/정정, 결함 허용, 결맞음 오류, 파울리 트와일링, 잡음 조정(noise tailoring). There are three small problems. In [5], the hedge "in part because" was dropped, so the continuum becomes the only reason the concepts are hard to tell apart. In [4] and [10], the English em-dash asides were copied into Korean, which reads stiffly; in [10] this also loses "어떤" in the "which ones typically cannot" clause. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: These concepts can be difficult to distinguish, in part because they lie along a continuum
examples.translation: 연속적인 스펙트럼 위에 놓여 있기 때문에 구분하기 어려울 수 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 연속적인 스펙트럼 위에 놓여 있다는 점도 한 이유가 되어 구분하기 어려울 수 있습니다.
examples.why: The qualifier 'in part' was dropped, so a partial reason now reads as the only reason.

examples.source: The computation demonstrates a quantum separation — providing superior efficiency, cost-effectiveness, or accuracy compared with classical methods alone.
examples.translation: 계산이 양자 분리—고전적 방법만으로는 얻을 수 없는 우수한 효율성, 비용 효율성 또는 정확성을 제공하는—를 보여줍니다.
examples.suggested: 계산이 양자 분리를 보여줍니다. 즉, 고전적 방법만 사용할 때보다 더 우수한 효율성, 비용 효율성 또는 정확성을 제공합니다.
examples.why: The em-dash aside embedded mid-sentence is a calque of English syntax and hard to read in Korean.

examples.source: which methods can be combined effectively within a single workflow — and which ones typically cannot.
examples.translation: 어떤 방법들을 효과적으로 조합할 수 있는지—그리고 일반적으로 조합할 수 없는지도 강조합니다.
examples.suggested: 어떤 방법들을 효과적으로 조합할 수 있고, 어떤 방법들은 일반적으로 함께 쓰기 어려운지도 짚어 봅니다.
examples.why: Without a second '어떤', the contrast between combinable and non-combinable methods is blurred, and the dash construction reads stiffly.

editor_note: Entry 11, the Credly privacy notice, matches the English in meaning. It keeps the data shared (이름, 이메일 주소, 취득한 배지), the US location, the "may share" hedge (공유할 수 있습니다) and the privacy-statement link, and it adds and drops nothing. The one thing a native editor would change is "instructions for claiming the badge", rendered as "배지를 청구하는 방법". 청구 is a word-for-word rendering of "claim" and means demanding payment or billing. For a badge, Korean uses 수령하다 or 받다. The formal 합니다체 with 귀하 is defensible for a legal notice and matches the rest of the page, so it is not flagged.

examples.source: You will receive an email notification from Credly with instructions for claiming the badge.
examples.translation: 배지를 청구하는 방법에 대한 안내가 담긴 이메일 알림을 Credly로부터 받게 됩니다.
examples.suggested: Credly에서 배지 수령 방법을 안내하는 이메일 알림을 받게 됩니다.
examples.why: 청구 (claim) is used for billing or demanding payment, which is odd for a badge. Korean uses 수령 or 받기 for claiming a badge.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries misleads a learner. The 16%/9% trade-off (36), the positive/negative sign convention (35), the remap_to_contiguous explanation (34) and the caveat that SABRE matches or beats the AI transpiler on some circuits (39, rendered with -기도) all keep their meaning. Entry 7 breaks the page's terminology: it writes '2-큐비트 깊이, 게이트 수', but the rest of the page, including entries 36 and 39, uses '두 Qubit 깊이' and 'Gate 수'. In entry 36, '더 적은 두 Qubit Gate의 순차적 레이어' can be read as 'fewer two-qubit gates', which blurs the depth-versus-count distinction the paragraph is teaching. The colon after '강조합니다:' is also a calque of the English punctuation.

examples.source: in terms of two-qubit depth, gate count, and transpilation time
examples.translation: 2-큐비트 깊이, 게이트 수, 트랜스파일 시간 측면에서
examples.suggested: 두 Qubit 깊이, Gate 수, 트랜스파일 시간 측면에서
examples.why: Every other entry, including the rewritten 36 and 39, uses '두 Qubit' and 'Gate'. Entry 7 alone switches to '2-큐비트' and '게이트', so the terms are inconsistent within the page.

examples.source: prioritizes depth reduction (fewer sequential layers of two-qubit gates)
examples.translation: 깊이 감소(더 적은 두 Qubit Gate의 순차적 레이어)를 우선시하는
examples.suggested: 깊이 감소(두 Qubit Gate의 순차적 레이어 수 감소)를 우선시하는
examples.why: '더 적은' can attach to '두 Qubit Gate', giving 'fewer two-qubit gates'. That muddies the depth-versus-gate-count contrast the paragraph sets up, since here the AI transpiler actually produces more gates.

examples.source: This highlights a key trade-off when choosing between the two strategies: the AI-powered transpiler...
examples.translation: 이는 두 전략 중 선택할 때의 주요 절충점을 강조합니다: AI 기반 Transpiler는...
examples.suggested: 이는 두 전략 중 하나를 고를 때 고려해야 할 핵심 절충점을 보여 줍니다. AI 기반 Transpiler는...
examples.why: The colon carried over from English after a finished Korean sentence is translationese; a native writer would end the sentence or rephrase.

editor_note: Entry 64 is faithful and natural: "가짜 백엔드로 AQC 최적화 회로와 기준 Trotter 회로를 모두 실행하여 ZZ 관측량을 측정하기 위해 EstimatorV2 프리미티브를 사용합니다" keeps both circuits, the fake backend and the ZZ observable, and it uses the file's terms 관측량, 기준 회로 and 프리미티브 consistently.

Both rewritten entries are faithful: entry 7 keeps "multiple observables … in a single call" as "한 번 호출하여 … 여러 관측량의 기댓값", and entry 38 keeps "sweeps the measurement basis of the first qubit" and "many parameter values in a single call" (한 번의 호출로 많은 매개변수 값에서), using the same 관측량/기댓값/매개변수화된/스윕 terms as the rest of the page.

All three rewritten entries are faithful. Entry 39 keeps the SamplerV2 / StatevectorSampler (qiskit.primitives, 로컬 시뮬레이션) distinction, entry 50 keeps both the "대략 지수적으로" hedge and the "아주 작은 문제 크기를 넘어서면" caveat, and entry 52 renders near-term as 단기(near-term) in both places.
Entry 17 is faithful and reads naturally: "참조 상태", "실시간 진화된 상태로부터 Krylov 부분공간을 구성합니다" match the source, and 해밀토니안 is used the same way as in the rest of the page.

I found no meaning errors in the four rewritten entries (0, 1, 28, 119). Entry 119 keeps the claim that the exact-static MPF (‖x‖₁ = 4.66) is the worst estimator and that capping the norm gives the best estimate. Entry 0 renders time-evolution as '시간 진화', but every other entry on the page uses '시간 전개' (전개 시간, 시간 전개 연산자), so the page's summary line uses a different term from its body. Entry 119 has some stiff, calqued phrasing: '모든 것 중 가장 나쁜 추정치' and especially '이 압도 효과가 사라지고', a literal rendering of 'removes this overwhelm' that a Korean technical writer would rephrase. Entry 28 is faithful and natural.

examples.source: implement time-evolution with fixed Trotter error in lower depth
examples.translation: 낮은 깊이에서 고정된 Trotter 오차로 시간 진화를 구현합니다
examples.suggested: 더 낮은 깊이에서 고정된 Trotter 오차로 시간 전개를 구현합니다
examples.why: Every other entry on the page uses '시간 전개' (e.g. [16], [28], [41]). '시간 진화' here makes the summary line inconsistent with the body.

examples.source: Capping the norm ... removes this overwhelm and gives the best estimate
examples.translation: 노름을 제한하면(근사-정적 솔버, $\|x\|_1 \approx 2$) 이 압도 효과가 사라지고 최선의 추정치를 제공합니다
examples.suggested: 노름을 제한하면(근사-정적 솔버, $\|x\|_1 \approx 2$) 이러한 노이즈 증폭이 억제되어 가장 좋은 추정치를 얻습니다
examples.why: '이 압도 효과가 사라지고' is a literal calque of 'removes this overwhelm' and reads stiffly. The meaning is correct.

examples.source: is the *worst* estimator of all
examples.translation: 모든 것 중 가장 나쁜 추정치입니다
examples.suggested: 모든 추정치 중 *가장 나쁩니다*
examples.why: '모든 것 중' is a stiff word-for-word rendering of 'of all', and the source's italic emphasis on 'worst' is dropped.

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries (8, 16, 62, 64, 74, 76) would mislead a learner. The key claims all match the English: the critical point is near 0.3π without noise, noise shifts it higher ("더 높은 쪽으로 이동"), the transition is still observed while it stays below 0.5π ("0.5π 미만"), and the peak sits at the edge of the sweep "경계 또는 그 너머로". Two small polish items remain. In entry 74, "resolve" is rendered as "분해(식별)할 수 있는", a hedging gloss in parentheses that a native editor would reduce to one word such as "구별할 수 있는". In entries 62 and 64, the lead-in to the display formula ends in a finished sentence plus a comma ("살펴볼 수 있습니다,"), which copies the English "defined as ..." structure and reads awkwardly in Korean.

examples.source: so the transition is at the edge of what this sweep can resolve.
examples.translation: 전이는 이 스윕으로 분해(식별)할 수 있는 한계에 있습니다.
examples.suggested: 전이는 이 스윕으로 구별할 수 있는 범위의 한계에 걸쳐 있습니다.
examples.why: The parenthetical double rendering '분해(식별)' is a translator's hedge left in the text. A native technical writer would pick one word.

examples.source: you can examine the average two-point correlation $f$, defined as
examples.translation: 다음과 같이 정의된 평균 2점 상관 $f$를 살펴볼 수 있습니다,
examples.suggested: 평균 2점 상관 $f$를 살펴볼 수 있습니다. $f$는 다음과 같이 정의됩니다.
examples.why: A finished Korean sentence followed by a comma leading into the display formula copies the English syntax. Entry 64 has the same pattern ('살펴볼 수 있습니다,' then '이는 ...').

editor_note: None of the six rewritten entries (14, 47, 49, 50, 51, 52) would mislead a learner. The m=9 to n=3 example, the O(m^{1/2}) compression, "k>1인 k체 상관관계는 k차 다항식 압축", the three measurement settings and the sign-based partition and swap-search steps all match the English. There are two small edits a native editor would make. In entry 14, the phrase "2체 Pauli 행렬 상관관계로서 최적화 문제를 상관관계 행렬로 나타냅니다" follows the English syntax too closely and stacks two "~로" phrases. In entry 52, "solution" becomes "솔루션", but entries 14 and 16 use "해" for the same concept.

examples.source: representing the optimization problem as a correlation matrix — specifically, two-body Pauli-matrix correlations across n=3 qubits
examples.translation: $n=3$ qubit $(Q_1, Q_2, Q_3)$에 걸친 2체(two-body) Pauli 행렬 상관관계로서 최적화 문제를 상관관계 행렬로 나타냅니다.
examples.suggested: 최적화 문제를 상관관계 행렬, 구체적으로는 $n=3$개 qubit $(Q_1, Q_2, Q_3)$에 걸친 2체(two-body) Pauli 행렬 상관관계로 나타냅니다.
examples.why: The appositive is squeezed into a '~로서' phrase ahead of the object. This stacks two '~로' phrases and hides the 'specifically' refinement, so the sentence reads stiffly.

examples.source: to improve the solution as a classical post-processing step
examples.translation: 단일 비트 스왑 탐색을 한 번 수행하여 솔루션을 개선합니다.
examples.suggested: 단일 비트 스왑 탐색을 한 번 수행하여 해를 개선합니다.
examples.why: Entries 14 and 16 render 'solution' as the mathematical term '해'. Switching to the loanword '솔루션' here is inconsistent within the page.

editor_note: None of the 14 rewritten entries misleads: the caveats in entries 51 and 66 (uncut circuits need many SWAP gates, no error suppression or mitigation was used, results could improve further) are kept, and 절단/가중치-1/Z형 관측량 are used consistently. Entry 66 says the cause twice ("Gate 절단을 통해 … 주기적 Gate를 절단했을 때 크게 향상"), which is clumsy and redundant. Entry 45 changes the purpose clause slightly: "개선만을 확인하기 위해" means "to observe only the improvement", while the English says DD and twirling are turned off so that any improvement comes solely from gate cutting.

examples.source: the average of the weight-1 ⟨Z⟩ and weight-2 ⟨ZZ⟩ type observables are significantly improved by cutting the periodic gates
examples.translation: Gate 절단을 통해 가중치-1 $\langle Z \rangle$ 및 가중치-2 $\langle ZZ \rangle$ 형 관측량의 평균이 주기적 Gate를 절단했을 때 크게 향상되었음을
examples.suggested: 주기적 Gate를 절단함으로써 가중치-1 $\langle Z \rangle$ 및 가중치-2 $\langle ZZ \rangle$ 형 관측량의 평균이 크게 향상되었음을
examples.why: The cause is stated twice (Gate 절단을 통해 … 절단했을 때), which reads as a stitched-together rewrite.

examples.source: so that any improvement we obtain in the result will solely be due to effective application of gate cutting
examples.translation: Gate 절단의 효과적인 적용으로 인한 개선만을 확인하기 위해
examples.suggested: 결과에서 얻는 개선이 오직 이 유형의 Circuit에 대한 Gate 절단의 효과적인 적용에서만 비롯되도록
examples.why: The English attributes the whole improvement to gate cutting alone. The Korean says 'to observe only the improvement from gate cutting', which is a slightly different purpose. It is not misleading, but it is less precise.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (13, 52, 61) say what the English says, and their terms match the rest of the page: 전역 상태 간의 겹침(overlap), 국소 관측량, 단일 큐비트 축약 밀도 행렬(1 RDM), 기댓값, 투영값, 방사 기저 함수(``'rbf'``) 커널. Entry 52 keeps the 80-minute QPU caveat and the note about the provided results.

Four of the five rewritten entries (7, 12, 45, 57) are accurate and read naturally. In entry 45, the "populate … (row 15, column 20)" step correctly becomes "커널 행렬 위치(행 15, 열 20)에 그 값을 채웁니다". Entry 28 translates "coset" two ways inside one paragraph: "코셋" in the problem name and the first sentence, which also matches entry 24, and "좌잉여류" for "left-cosets" at the end. A learner may not realize these are the same concept. Use "좌코셋" so the term stays consistent with the rest of the page. The math, the stabilizer condition and the Standard Model example keep their meaning.

examples.source: Finally, we define two left-cosets $C_\pm = c_\pm S_\text{graph}$ by drawing two $c_\pm \in G$ at random.
examples.translation: 마지막으로, 두 $c_\pm \in G$를 무작위로 추출하여 두 좌잉여류 $C_\pm = c_\pm S_\text{graph}$을 정의합니다.
examples.suggested: 마지막으로, 두 $c_\pm \in G$를 무작위로 추출하여 두 좌코셋 $C_\pm = c_\pm S_\text{graph}$을 정의합니다.
examples.why: The same paragraph and entry 24 use 코셋 for coset, but here it becomes 잉여류. Using two terms for one concept is inconsistent and could make a reader think left-cosets are something different.

editor_note: Neither rewritten entry changes the meaning. Entry 10 says the same thing as the English, but "이해하는 데 관련된 분자 수준의 통찰" copies the structure of "insight relevant to understanding" and reads stiffly in Korean. Entry 29 uses "파트 2", but the matching heading in entry 15 is still "Part 1", so the two part headings on the page don't match. Use the same form for both headings.

examples.source: Part 2: FeP-NO (44Q)
examples.translation: 파트 2: FeP-NO (44Q)
examples.suggested: Part 2: FeP-NO (44Q) (to match entry 15 'Part 1'), or change both headings to 파트 1/파트 2
examples.why: The two part headings are inconsistent: entry 15 leaves 'Part 1' in English, while entry 29 uses 파트 2.

examples.source: provides molecular-level insight relevant to understanding the chemical transformations in these systems
examples.translation: 이러한 시스템의 화학적 변화를 이해하는 데 관련된 분자 수준의 통찰을 얻을 수 있습니다
examples.suggested: 이러한 시스템에서 일어나는 화학적 변화를 이해하는 데 도움이 되는 분자 수준의 통찰을 얻을 수 있습니다
examples.why: '이해하는 데 관련된' is a literal copy of 'relevant to understanding' and sounds stiff. '도움이 되는' reads naturally. The meaning is faithful.

editor_note: All three rewritten entries (24, 53, 85) keep the English meaning. Each says a single echo is the default, the multi-echo CPMG variant comes at the end, dynamical decoupling suppresses low-frequency noise, and the total free-evolution time makes the results directly comparable. Nothing here would mislead a learner. Entry 85 has two small wording problems. The phrase "한 번의 Hahn 에코(단일 에코)만" says the same thing twice. The passive "위의 비교 플롯에서 보여진 것처럼" reads as a calque of the English. Entry 24 also uses an English-style semicolon ("사용됩니다; 다중 에코…") where a Korean writer would split the sentence or use a connective ending.

examples.source: By default the $T_2$ experiment applies a single Hahn echo and measures all qubits in parallel, which, as the comparison plot above showed,
examples.translation: 기본적으로 $T_2$ 실험은 한 번의 Hahn 에코(단일 에코)만 적용하고 모든 큐비트를 병렬로 측정하는데, 위의 비교 플롯에서 보여진 것처럼
examples.suggested: 기본적으로 $T_2$ 실험은 Hahn 에코를 한 번만 적용하고 모든 큐비트를 병렬로 측정하는데, 앞의 비교 플롯에서 본 것처럼
examples.why: The parenthetical '(단일 에코)' just repeats '한 번의 … 에코'. The passive '보여진 것처럼' is a calque of the English; '본 것처럼' is the natural Korean phrasing.

examples.source: By default a single echo is used; a multi-echo (CPMG-style) variant is demonstrated at the end of this tutorial.
examples.translation: 기본적으로 단일 에코가 사용됩니다; 다중 에코(CPMG 스타일) 변형은 이 튜토리얼의 끝에서 시연됩니다.
examples.suggested: 기본값은 단일 에코이며, 다중 에코(CPMG 방식) 변형은 이 튜토리얼 마지막 부분에서 다룹니다.
examples.why: The semicolon is carried over from English punctuation. Joining the clauses with a connective ending ('-이며') reads more naturally in Korean.
